title: Tag probe reactive (B): pending-join, park cursor on miss until matching write
description:
The reactive variant of sprefa-8h4. On probe miss, park cursor via Yield<TagWake> until a write to :name lands a row matching (X, Y). On match, wake + pass. On runtime cancel, drop.

# Builds on sprefa-8h4 (A)

A is a strict subset: A = sync lookup + drop on miss; B = sync lookup + park on miss + key-aware wake. The lookup primitive (TagStore::lookup_by_key) is shared. The probe op shell is shared.

# What B adds on top of A

1. **Keyed waiters.** Bag.waiters today: Vec<SubjectKey<TagWake>>; broadcast on every write. For B: HashMap<KeyTuple, Vec<SubjectKey<TagWake>>>; only wake waiters whose probed key equals the new row's key. Otherwise N×M wasted wakes.

2. **Writer wake by key.** TagWriteBatcher derives the row's key (which columns count toward identity? all? a declared subset?), looks up matching waiters, fires next() on each. Open: column-identity contract.

3. **Probe-miss path.** Op state machine: lookup_by_key -> if hit, emit; if miss, fresh_key + register waiter under the probed (X,Y) tuple, park via Yield<TagWake>. On wake, emit. On cancel, drop.

# Reuses already-landed runtime

- Yield<TagWake> typed coroutine (sprefa-7e5)
- SubjectRegistry<TagWake>::subscribe synchronous race-safe registration (sprefa-944)
- TagWriteBatcher fan-out broadcast pattern (extend to keyed)
- TagStore::snapshot_or_subscribe atomic store-lock-then-subscribe pattern (extend to keyed)

# Design opens

- Column-identity for keyed wakes: all columns? Declared key prefix? Inferred from probe shape?
- Augment vs predicate: if probe is rule(:n, $X, ${Y?}), do we still ban ? in pipe position (per user)? If no augment, probes are predicates only.
- Multi-row match semantics: fan-out (one cursor per matching row) or pick-one?

- v3/crates/pipeline/src/effects.rs — Bag.waiters HashMap + push_row by-key wake
- v3/crates/pipeline/src/ops/tag.rs — Probe-miss park branch
- new tests for park/wake-on-key-match + drop-on-cancel

title: Tag probe op (A): static lookup-by-bound-key, pass-or-drop
description:
The all-bound, no-body, pipe-position form: rule(:name, $X, $Y) — probe the bag for rows matching (X, Y). Cursor passes if any row matches, dropped if none. Static (sync) variant of the future reactive pending-join.

Open dispatch question: today TagOp::from_values classifies all-bound as Write. Adding Probe needs a discriminator. Candidates:
1. Top-level vs pipe-position context (lower path knows). Awkward.
2. Brace absence + presence of downstream op = probe; brace absence + no downstream = write. Implicit, fragile.
3. Reserve write semantics for rule-body-terminal sink emissions only; pipe-position bare tag(:n, $X) becomes probe. Breaks current tag(:hits, 'x') write call site.
4. New sigil/keyword (tag?(:n, $X) for probe). Visible, unambiguous.

Decision blocked on surface design session with user.

# Implementation (independent of dispatch decision)

Storage: TagStore::lookup_by_key(name, key: &[Arc<str>]) -> Vec<TagRow>. Sync, under one mutex acquisition.

Op:
  pipe(cursor) -> if lookup matches: pass cursor (optionally augmented with row data); else: drop.

# Test plan

- store has rows; probe with matching key passes cursor through.
- store has rows; probe with non-matching key drops cursor.
- store empty; probe drops.
- multi-row match: fan-out (or augment, per design).

title: Stream the runner: Op + Pipeline switch to BoxStream<Arc<[Cursor]>>
description:
Convert Op trait and Pipeline runner from Vec<Cursor>/BoxFuture<Vec<Cursor>> to a stream-to-stream shape, matching the v3 vision (RxJS Observable<Arc<[Cursor]>> -> Observable<Arc<[Cursor]>>).

Locked shape (session 20260426.4):

  trait Op {
    fn pipe(ctx, batch: Arc<[Cursor]>) -> BoxFuture<Arc<[Cursor]>> { identity }
    fn pipe_flat_map(ctx, upstream: BoxStream<Arc<[Cursor]>>) -> BoxStream<Arc<[Cursor]>> {
        upstream.map(|b| self.pipe(ctx, b)).buffer_unordered(64).boxed()  // mergeMap default
    }
  }

  Pipeline::run(ctx, upstream: BoxStream<Arc<[Cursor]>>) -> BoxStream<Arc<[Cursor]>>
    Op  -> op.pipe_flat_map(ctx, upstream).map(tag_PathSeg)
    Seq -> stages.iter().fold(upstream, |s, st| st.run(ctx, s))
    Fork-> broadcast upstream to N arms, merge arm streams

Backpressure: native via futures::Stream pull. buffer_unordered(N) caps in-flight and
parks upstream poll when full. No rxrust emulation needed.

Strategy choice: mergeMap(N) default. switchMap/exhaustMap are top-level driver
concerns (LSP rerun, debounce), not the op layer.

Port surface:
  - finite per-batch ops (write_cursor, comment, repo, rev, str, void, print,
    cursor_ref, render, json, re, glob, lsp): override pipe only, use default
    pipe_flat_map. Mostly mechanical conversion of existing pipe(Cursor)->Vec<Cursor>
    to pipe(Arc<[Cursor]>)->Arc<[Cursor]>.
  - bulk ops (ast_grep, read): override pipe with bulk inner pass.
  - fan-out ops (fs): override pipe_flat_map for walker fan-out.

PathSeg tagging stays runner-owned, applied as a stream map.

Tests:
  - existing op tests adapt to new pipe signature
  - new test: Pipeline::run streams batches lazily (not collected upfront)
  - new test: backpressure via buffer_unordered (N in-flight cap)
  - new test: Fork broadcast + merge order independence

title: Tag MVP — TagStore + TagOp + TagWrite/TagReadEffect using Yield
description:
Tag op MVP. Depends on sprefa-cld (stream runner) — TagReadOp's perpetual subscription is implemented as a pipe_flat_map override.

Semantics (locked 2026-04-26 session 20260426.4):
  - tag(:name, ...) — name is a literal symbol, then positional args
  - all args bound ($X already-defined captures or literals) -> WRITE: append row to bag :name
  - all args unbound (?X introducer) -> READ: drain current rows + perpetually subscribe
  - mixed bound/unbound -> LOWER ERROR
  - dynamic-arity bag: writers may use any column count; bag stores Vec<Vec<Arc<str>>> as-is
  - no filtering; reader gets every row past + future, captures bind positionally
  - row arity mismatch with reader capture count = user discipline; bind by zip, no padding

Effects:
  TagWriteEffect { name: Arc<str>, row: Vec<Arc<str>> }
    Batcher: lock store, push row, drain waiter SubjectKeys, registry.next on each.

Store:
  TagStore impl Store via TypeMap.
  inner: Mutex<HashMap<Arc<str>, Bag>>
  Bag { rows: Vec<Vec<Arc<str>>>, waiters: Vec<SubjectKey> }
  Atomic snapshot_or_subscribe(name) -> drains current rows OR registers waiter.

Ops:
  TagWriteOp: override pipe; for each cursor, materialize row (bound captures + literals),
              ctx.put(TagWriteEffect), pass cursor through unchanged.
  TagReadOp: override pipe_flat_map; for each cursor in each upstream batch:
             emit one batch with all current rows bound positionally, then
             loop { register fresh SubjectKey, ctx.put(Yield).await, emit row }
             until Unsubscribed.

Lowering:
  - Vec<Value> classification: first must be Atom (name); rest are Term/Atom/Literal
  - if any Term::Read among rest AND any Term::Unbound among rest -> error tag/mixed-mode
  - if all Term::Read or Atom/Literal -> WriteOp
  - if all Term::Unbound -> ReadOp
  - tag/missing-name, tag/non-atom-name diagnostics

Tests:
  1. write+read roundtrip same op: write 2 rows, then read drains both
  2. dynamic-arity: write [a,b] then [c,d,e], read with 2 captures binds first row's both, second row's first two
  3. read-then-write subscribe: read on empty bag yields, write later resolves
  4. unsubscribe on lineage retract / runtime cancel
  5. mixed-mode lower error

title: Effect-park primitive — writes pause until user approves; cancellable on upstream invalidation
description:
Architectural lock 2026-04-26: every write effect (WriteRangeEffect, WriteFileEffect, future SqlWriteEffect) is a parked operation requiring user approval before it executes. The park primitive is the same mechanism that powers tag-subscribe / Pending (sprefa-126) — generalized so any side-effect-with-durability flows through:

  ctx.put(WriteRangeEffect{...})
    └─► batcher receives effect, stashes in pending-queue (NOT executed)
        └─► UI/CLI surfaces pending writes
            └─► user approves a write or a batch
                └─► batcher executes against the actual sink (disk/sqlite/lsp-edit)

Cancellation: a pending write is invalidated if the upstream cursor lineage that produced it changes (e.g. file content edited, capture re-bound to different bytes, fs(glob) re-fans). Effect-runtime needs to track which cursor lineage produced each parked effect and cancel pending writes whose precondition no longer holds.

Why parked-by-default: writes are durable, mistakes are expensive, sprefa is a research/review tool not a YOLO formatter. User-as-gate is the design intent.

Two pieces:
  1. Generic Park<E> in effect_runtime — extends the EffectKind/Batcher pair with a 'pending' state. Writes return a ParkHandle; runner records (cursor_lineage_id, ParkHandle) for cancellation. Approve/cancel APIs on RtCtx.
  2. Per-effect approval policy — Effect trait grows IS_DURABLE constant; durable effects auto-park, ephemeral effects (PrintEffect, FsListFilesEffect) don't.

Spike — design session required before code lands.

4. Tag-as-op: lowerer-privileged op name. No grammar change.
5. Lineage: capture-level. CursorLineage { binding_origin, capture_id }.

description:

title: SQLite persistence for tag rows + rule exit-cursor collection
description:
Tag rows (variadic ArgTuples per :name) and rule exit-cursor sets both need a durable backing store so:
- Tag replays across sprefa-run invocations without re-enumerating sources.
- Rules can collect their exit cursors (the set of cursor-lineages that reached the rule's terminal yield point) for querying and cross-repo analysis.

Rule exit-cursor collection is load-bearing: a rule def declares a yield point; cursors flowing through the rule call are streamed into the rule body, and the body's terminal emits exit cursors. Downstream code that wants to iterate all cursors that reached rule :foo needs a way to enumerate them.

May require op event-surface update: rule body ops need a hook to notify 'this cursor reached the terminal yield' so the store can record it. Candidate: a new OpEvent variant on the existing op event surface, or a wrapper op (RuleExitSink) that the lower path auto-inserts at rule-body terminals.

Schema sketch (SQLite):
  tag_rows     (tag_name TEXT, col_idx INT, value BLOB, row_id INT, written_at INT)
  rule_exits   (rule_name TEXT, cursor_id BLOB, sprf_path TEXT, captures_json BLOB)

Open design questions:
- In-memory first (Arc<TagStore> + Arc<RuleExitStore>) with SQLite as flush-on-exit? Or SQLite live?
- Cursor identity for exit collection: SprfPath + captures hash? UUID per cursor? Deterministic across runs?
- Rule terminal detection: does the lower path know which Op is 'the last in a rule body'? Probably yes via a RuleBody wrapper frame.

Unlocks:
- Query 'all exits of rule :foo' as a first-class language operation.
- Cross-run memoization (don't re-scan unchanged repos).
- Cross-repo analysis via rule joining (sprefa-4m7.13).

title: Source-op arg-pipe contract — repo/rev/fs consume last_bound uniformly
description:
Lock the shape of source ops (repo, rev, fs) around a single contract: each takes an arg-pipe that produces cursors; the op sets its cursor-field (repo/rev/fs) from each output cursor's `last_bound` value and streams the decorated cursor downstream.

Uniform shape:
  repo(arg_pipe) — for each cursor c emitted by arg_pipe: c.repo := c.last_bound; emit c.
  rev(arg_pipe)  — same, cursor.rev.
  fs(arg_pipe)   — same, cursor.fs.

Arg-pipe producers:
  str(main)                  — yields one cursor with last_bound = 'main'
  glob(~/projects/*.git)     — yields N cursors, last_bound = path per match
  tag(:repo, ${REPO?})      — yields N cursors, last_bound = REPO value per tag row
  { > A ; > B }              — fork merges producers, last_bound preserved through each arm

Arg-pipe terminal requirements:
- Must be an op that writes last_bound (str, glob, tag, etc.).
- Bare `${REPO?}` terminal = rejected by BindingGraph if nothing in the arm binds REPO.
- Per-op well-formedness check (in the op's lower path) decides whether 'no arg' is acceptable:
  - repo() with no arg → default enumeration (config-dir walk).
  - rev() with no arg → error; rev requires a concrete filter (per user lock).
  - fs() with no arg → default cwd walk.

SprfPath:
- Arg-pipe gets its own path sub-tree. Cursors from arg-pipe live at <op_name>/arg[0]/<inner_path>.
- Enumerated values get value-indexed segments for stability across runs (memoization hook).
- Single-arm fork inside arg-pipe is kept at runtime identity (not parse-collapsed) so SprfPath arm is visible.

Reason: unifies the three cursor-field ops around one contract, makes enumeration/filtering/seeding compositional, falls cleanly out of already-existing mechanics (last_bound, Fork, arg-pipes). No new trait axes needed.

- All bound → push row (ArgTuple) to the :name BehaviorSubject. No fan, cursor unchanged.
- Any ${X?} → subscribe to :name, fan one cursor per existing row matching bound positions, bind ${X?} from row. Remain subscribed; future writes retroactively wake and fan.
- Schema: variadic per call site. Arity locks on first write of a given :name; later arity mismatch = diagnostic.

Tag is a language primitive (grammar-level recognition at parse-head position), not a stdlib op. Its storage is internal: HashMap<TagName, BehaviorSubject<ArgTuple>>. Bound/unbound dispatch lives in tag's own lower path, not in the general Op trait surface.

Explicit writes only. Op enumerators (repo, fs, etc.) do NOT auto-publish to tags; if user wants a tag populated from enumeration, they fork a tag-write arm:
  repo({ > glob(...) ; > tag(:repo, ${REPO}) ; })

Composition: tag calls nest freely inside other carveouts, e.g.:
  repo(re(support/${tag(:foo, ${A?})}))
evaluates the inner tag read per outer cursor, substitutes the bound value into the regex template.

Retires: is_repo, is_rev, is_fs, is_repo_norm, is_rev_norm, link(:kind, ...), and `is` as a distinct primitive. Tag covers all cases via its variadic arity and bound/unbound dispatch. Append-log semantics (what `is` offered) fall out of BehaviorSubject replay — every row is retained and replayed to new subscribers.

**Trio review findings 2026-04-23**

- Bootstrap vs live distinction needed. Tag on startup loads historic rows into a 'cold store' queried synchronously by subscribers; live writes flow through BehaviorSubject as events. New subscriber: read cold-store snapshot, then attach to Subject for future. Avoids N-row replay storm and avoids replay triggering downstream sh side-effects.
- Subscribe-during-write race: resolved by Arc<RwLock> snapshot-before-push. Iterate snapshot of subscriber list; new subscribers see cold-store during init, attach for future emits only.
- String-template context: when tag/sh/re takes a string-literal arg with ${X} interpolation slots, carveout content inside the string lowers to an interpolate(X) read, not a term-op call. Context-sensitive. Lock before sh lands.

title: Cursor-local Pending capture — same-pipe park on missing term
description:
Narrowed from original 4-mechanic synthesis. Scope now: wait state that lives on the cursor's own Capture entry, wake within the same cursor lineage.

Data shape:
  enum CaptureState { Bound(Value), Pending(Subject<Value>) }

Behavior:
- An unbound-read ${X?} hits a Capture slot. If no entry, create Pending with a fresh Subject.
- An unbound-read ${X?} in a sibling op that introduces the binding fires the Subject, wakes the parked reader, Capture transitions to Bound.
- Cursor lineage is respected: clones share the Subject, so Fork arm A's park can be woken by arm B's write on the same cursor (pre-fork) or by a downstream write back up into the lineage.

OUT OF SCOPE (handled elsewhere):
- Cross-pipe merge / xref-style OR semantics → structural via `;` Fork, no runtime primitive needed.
- Tag read/write / retroactive wake → owned inside the tag op's own BehaviorSubject storage (sprefa-bsa).
- Parametric rule lazy unbound → owned inside rule call-site / def-site machinery (sprefa-4m7.5.1).
- Scan-pointer Tri verification → retired (superseded by bidir tag + wait mechanic).

Before this narrowing, the spike contemplated a unified global label registry keyed by WaitKey discriminator. The registry idea is dropped: the three consumers (tag, rule, cursor) each own their own subject storage with different semantics (BehaviorSubject replay vs event-stream vs per-lineage park). Trying to unify them added a crosscutting abstraction that simplified nothing.

This card now only owns (1) the Capture::Pending state + (2) the lineage-local Subject wiring.

Implementation seam: pipeline crate (Cursor + Capture).

title: SPIKE: Pattern IS Op — unify pattern/pipeline/tuple/struct under single trait
description:
Patterns, pipelines, tuples, and structs all share the shape 'list-of-cursors -> list-of-cursors'. If Pattern::compile returns Arc<dyn Op>, Value collapses to a single Op variant (plus Tuple if a const-shape concession is kept). Bulk-path specialization (e.g. fs driving a compiled regex in batch) becomes Any-downcast at the outer op's discretion, not a separate Value variant.

Thesis artifacts:
- tuple (A, B, C) = Seq[A, B, C] = A > B > C (pipe) at the AST level
- struct { f: v, g: w } = Seq[set(f, v), set(g, w)] emitting a record cursor (allocation-over-time)
- $TERM = term(X) op = identity-with-capture-bind
- patterns with unbound terms = ops with non-empty free-variable set; evaluating requires a body (why rev($V) is rejected: term-only into filter semantic has nothing to bind from)

Tradeoffs to explore:
- Op trait object-safety vs bulk-path specialization via Any (already the current posture, §14.2b)
- Registry factory signature: does it still need Vec<Value> or does a single Arc<dyn Op> per slot suffice? (probably still tuple for n-ary)
- Do we keep Pattern as a named concept at all, or does it evaporate into 'Op with the PatternOp extension trait'?

description:

No stream-aggregation. No count. Just scalar compare on the current cursor.

ast vs cst op split (2026-04-22): tree-sitter grammar dispatch is build-time, so dynamic grammar picks inside a bracket slot are impossible. Factoring: ast[$LANG](...) takes ast-grep pattern-by-example syntax (sweet spot: code-shaped patterns like TODO($ISSUE)); cst[$LANG](...) takes tree-sitter query S-expressions (sweet spot: structural one-liners like (string_literal) @S). Both compile to Value::Pattern(Pattern::Ast) with different confirm strategies. Sub-grammar inside each is lang-agnostic at source, lang-resolved at pattern-compile via tree-sitter language blob load. CST is the accurate name: tree-sitter produces a lossless CST, ast-grep is a pattern-by-example layer on top. Strings indexer recipe uses cst[$LANG]((string_literal) @S) as the cleaner form; ast[$LANG] is the form for content-shaped matches. Filed 2.28.

Pattern-op position duality + nestable ast/cst (locked 2026-04-22, parse.md §14.2b §14.2c): same PatternOp::compile produces Pattern value used in two ways. At pipe-step it drives Op::pipe -> Pattern::apply. At arg slot it is Value::Pattern the outer op introspects. Choice lives entirely in host lowerer via outer op's ArgSpec. Nested ast/cst: second structural op re-parses the narrowed cursor.content[byte_range] per §14.5b content contract; same mechanic as any pipe-step chain. Brace-block sugar 'ast(outer){ > ast(inner); > ... }' desugars to linear chain; exists for readability. Pattern ops carry no special status in the pipe - they emit cursors, downstream consumes.
